terms.meaning: The study of society. The word comes from Latin "Socius" and Greek "Logos".
The process of learning language, behaviour and ways of thinking by living among people.
How human society is described, since people exist through their ties with others.
A person who studies society, culture, behaviour and social relationships.

items.name: August Comte's definition
items.formula: The scientific study of what relates to social order and social progress.
items.example: He first used the word Sociology.

items.name: MacIver and Page's definition
items.example: Shorter than Comte's, and focused on relationships.

items.name: Why study sociology
items.formula: Personality development, solving social problems, knowing modern developments.
items.example: It also promotes the welfare of weaker sections.

items.name: Why man is a social being
items.formula: No society without man, and no man without society.
items.example: Nobody could live all alone in a town.

items.name: Who socialises us
items.formula: Family, school, peer groups and mass communication.
items.example: School gives formal education; peers teach co-operation.

items.name: Kamala of Midnapore
items.formula: Found in 1920 after 9 years among animals; she walked on all fours and ate raw flesh.
items.example: It shows that without society a person doesn't develop human ways.

items.name: Language and human life
items.formula: Language separates man from animals and lets us express exact relationships and feelings.
items.example: Without it there would be no schools, mass media or civilization.

items.name: Father of Sociology
items.example: He named the scientific study of society.

items.name: Herbert Spencer
items.example: He studied the evolution of society.

items.name: Emile Durkheim
items.example: He worked to make sociology a science.

items.name: Max Weber
items.formula: A German sociologist, also a scholar of economics, philosophy and history.
items.example: He studied the labour force and the Christian religion.

items.name: Karl Marx
items.formula: A German philosopher, learned in history and economics.
items.example: He extended the scope of sociology.

items.name: Sociology in India
items.formula: The British introduced it at Bombay University in 1914.
items.example: G. S. Ghurye, M. N. Srinivas, A. R. Desai, Iravati Karve and S. C. Dubey are leading names.

mistakes.text: "Socius" is Latin and "Logos" is Greek, so the word has two language roots.
Kamala learnt to speak only later, among people. Language comes through society, not by itself.
Family and peers socialise us too, so socialization is not only what school does.
